Are there still any brave hearts left to shield and defend?
Does even a single spark of hope still flicker?
Who stands guard over this forest and shore—our silent protector?

When the red feathers flutter, weary from pain,
And courage dissolves into sorrow within the mighty river,
Who becomes the sun that rises even through the night to comfort us?

When the land begins to crumble within the burning fence,
And the skies pour down, breaking in despair,

Is there memory to guide us? Courage in our hearts? A dream that stirs? A fire that burns?
Let this fractured land awaken as one, united.

Let us stand together beneath one sky, as one people.

Who will come with steady hands to pull the poison out?
Is there still a healer left who knows how to ease the pain?

When the wind halts, frozen in the fog,
And burning coals fade into the folds of memory,
Is there a god who will warm our nights and lull us to rest with song?
Who rules this nation now, and who will whisper truth into our ears?

Is there memory to guide us? Courage in our hearts? A dream that stirs? A fire that burns?
Let this fractured land awaken as one, united.
